headline: South Asia: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen.
- India: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
- Western Russia: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
Ret. Army Gen. David Petraeus praised the Pentagon’s new Autonomous Warfare Command but said the U.S. must rapidly prepare for modern autonomous war.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
Government senator Marlon Morgan has called for the reintroduction of criminal sanctions for defamation in Jamaica. Making his contribution to the State of the Nation Debate in the Upper House on Friday, Morgan took aim at the parliamentary Opposition and those he referred to as their surrogates and supporters on social media, blasting them for tarnishing people’s reputation. He warned that the misinformation and disinformation being peddled by these persons serve to undermine the country’s democracy.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: PATHWAYS MURDER TRIAL | Second JP backs claim Ruddock was not forced to give statement.
A second justice of the peace (JP) on Friday testified that Andre Ruddock voluntarily gave police a statement in which he allegedly confessed to cutting Taneka Gardner’s throat. The witness corroborated earlier testimony from a colleague that Ruddock was not forced, threatened or harmed, nor offered any inducement to give the caution statement, on October 18, 2021 – a day after Gardner was killed in an alleged sacrificial ritual at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: What to know about AI-detected Internet security bug.
AP: The language that’s known as the backbone of the Internet is now subject to what experts describe as one of the most notable vulnerabilities in recent memory. PHP is a widely used general-purpose scripting language that is geared toward web development, and thus, it powers the majority of websites around the world. When the organisation behind the language and the Federal Bureau of Investigations’ cyber division warned Wednesday of significant vulnerabilities in the language, government agencies, corporations and other organisations were sent into a flurry.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast killed four people and injured 14, including an 11-year-old girl.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Three firefighters injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv – photo.
Russian forces attacked Kharkiv with drones on the evening of 24 October. Four people, including three firefighters, were injured in the strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: One killed and five injured in Russian drone strike on bus in Kherson – photos.
Kherson City Military Administration has reported six civilian casualties after a Russian drone hit a passenger-filled bus on the afternoon of 25 October.
- The Moscow Times, one hour ago: Ukrainian Attacks Kill 5 in Belgorod and Lipetsk, Hit Perm Industrial Plant.
Four people were killed in southwestern Russia’s Belgorod region and one in the Lipetsk region.

On June 13, 2025, the Mossad released sensational and rare video footage of its co-lead role with the air force in Israel's preemptive strike on Iran's ballistic missiles and air defenses.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: How is the US-Israeli war on Iran causing havoc in Europe?.
Rising energy costs and protests are sharpening European opposition to renewed US-Israeli attacks on Iran.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: CENTCOM reportedly has plans for Iran strikes: Will Trump approve them?.
Reports say Pentagon has drawn up plans for strikes after midterm polls, but analysts question what it could achieve.
Africa - bottom line: Iranian president blames United States for failure of interim peace deal.
- Africanews, 3 hours ago: Iranian president blames United States for failure of interim peace deal.
Masoud Pezeshkian emphasised, however, that a new attempt should be made to reach an agreement to end the war with the US and Israel.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Africanews, The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen.
Yemen’s Houthi rebels launched wide-ranging strikes across swathes of southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday, as the kingdom announced the partial reopening of Riyadh’s international airport despite repeated attacks by the group. Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted. Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Jerusalem Post, NDTV - Top Stories, just now: The nuclear danger at sea.
Dawn’s October 23 editorial rightly warned about India’s nuclear-armed submarine patrols. The danger is larger than a new vessel at sea. It is a sea-based nuclear force growing alongside precision-strike capabilities, missile defence and a false confidence in initiating military action. Imagining that these developments confer a first-strike advantage or create a safe space for war is imprudent. Pakistan has the capability and resolve to preserve the strategic balance.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Israeli strike on Gaza university kills 3; another 4 Palestinians killed in other attacks.
An Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday, staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported four others killed elsewhere in the territory. Reached for comment, the Israeli military said it was looking into the reports. Al Shifa Hospital said it received three bodies and treated eight people who were wounded in the Gaza City drone strike, with two sources at the Islamic University saying those killed were administrative staff and the injured were students.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump.
Relations between United States President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticising the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump’s frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv’s supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Ukraine hits back at Musk’s claim over civilian Starlink use for offensive strikes.
Ukraine's military firmly dismissed Elon Musk's claims that Starlink was used for offensive drone strikes. A Ukrainian defence technology adviser confirmed that limitations prevented such usage, countering Musk's assertions. Connectivity issues have further hampered military efforts amid ongoing Russian assaults, prompting renewed diplomatic engagement. Concurrently, Ukraine faces a surge in drone strikes on its urban centers.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: 'Wars Being Fought By Attacking Economies': PM Modi On "Cyber Terrorists".

Before the outbreak of the war triggered by the US-Israeli attack on Iran in February, the Gulf monarchies were living the prosperity dream that was the envy of the world. Their hydrocarbon-fuelled economies were glitzy oases of growth, inoculated from the conflict in Gaza that had rocked other parts of the Middle East for several years. China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier strike group sailed beyond the first island chain last week to reach the southernmost waters of the Philippines, suggesting an intent to position itself closer to ongoing US-Japan joint exercises. Philippine news channel BNC reported that the carrier group reached about 25 nautical miles (46km) east-southeast of Balut Island, the southernmost point of the Philippines, before sailing northeast on Friday. Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Kim Jong Un says North Korea ‘inspired’ by China’s success in border city visit.
- NK News, 17 hours ago: Kim Jong Un says North Korea ‘inspired’ by China’s success in border city visit.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said his country is “inspired” by China’s success during a visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday marking the 76th anniversary of China entering the Korean War, according to DPRK state media. AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Another Perth beach closed as more whale remains found.
- ABC News Australia, 12 hours ago: Another Perth beach closed as more whale remains found.
All beaches in Sorrento, where a man was attacked and killed by a great white shark last month, have been closed after a whale's tail was found offshore.
- The Guardian - Australia, 22 hours ago: The BoM’s temperature record keeping is under attack – again. What’s going on? | Temperature Check.
An ‘audit’ of the Bureau of Meteorology main dataset for measuring climate change claims it contains ‘widespread errors’. It doesn’t stack up Want to get this in your inbox when it publishes? Sign up for the Clear Air Australia newsletter here Australia’s climate has warmed by more than 1.5C since 1910, according to the Bureau of Meteorology’s main long-term temperature data. If you were so motivated, you might think if you could discredit this data, then you would undermine the whole climate change story and even – perhaps – the rationale for cutting Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions.
